utterances.text: Did Mr. Landzo say anything to this man (redacted)when he was doing these things?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He would insult him and yell at him, curse him, do all kinds of things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did at any time this man, (redacted), receive medical attention for the burns he had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He got some medical attention only when the Red Cross came. As far as I can remember the Red Cross came and they saw these people and then they ordered that some medical aid be given to them and then they appointed a doctor, I think Relja Mrkajic and Petko, they were in number 2 and they went over there to have bandages put on them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These instances when you say (redacted) was burnt, did they happen inside the hangar or both inside and outside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There was inside and outside, he would do it inside and outside; both inside and out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again "he" referring there to Mr. Landzo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Landzo, Mr. Landzo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say gunpowder as well, what do you mean by that, "gunpowder as well".

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think something yellowish. I would see the children would take it out of the bullets. It looked like something yellowish so I thought it was gunpowder.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This was flammable so far as you know? It would light up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly. He was carrying something in his hand, it might have been a liquid, but in any event it was burning, so I do not know. How can I decide? I know it was burning, there was a flame.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know a prisoner in the camp called Mirko Babic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did, I knew Mirko Babic, he was a forester, an elderly man. He worked in Sipad as well, as a carpenter.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you approximately tell us his age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mirko Babic, I do not know exactly now, but close to 60, something like that, 58, 60. I do not know exactly, but round about that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was his ethnic group, are you able to say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: A Serb, he was a Serb, too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you observe how he was treated by Mr. Delic and Mr. Landzo during the period of time that you were in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They beat him, they took him out, inside also they beat him. He was sitting there, they would hit him. They beat him just like they beat the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again while you were in the camp, did you come to know a prisoner -- did you know a prisoner by the name of Nedeljko Draganic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did know Nedeljko Draganic, too. His father was Rajko Draganic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know him before you went into the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him before I arrived at the camp. He is my uncle's son.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything happen to him in the camp while you were there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The same things happened to him, too. He was taken out by Zenga, by Kemo, by Osman and Delic, too, occasionally but mostly these others would take him out. Zenga would force him to graze grass, to eat grass, where people had urinated, and he had to do it. He had to lick something, that is what he told us in the hangar. These things were happening outside. On one occasion he was taken out and now I cannot exactly recall, but his trousers were burnt and he had two burns after that on his leg.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see these burns when he came back into the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those burns could be seen later because the trousers had -- the legs of the trousers had burnt and you could see the naked flesh on his legs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see whether or not he received medical attention for these burns?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not get any medical attention, only when the Red Cross came and they asked the people, when they came they asked individually when they would see these things on certain people. They would ask and then they demanded that they be treated and bandaged.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The time that he was taken out and received these burns, that is what you observed when he came back. Do you know who it was that took him out on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zenga did this most. There was something that was burning and then he would pour something on him. His trousers were burning and then somehow they put it off so his leg got scorched. You could hear his moans.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you also know a prisoner by the name of Vukasin Mrkajic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew Vukasin Mrkajic, too. He, too, was insulted and beaten. He would start doing pushups and they would hit him and he would fall and cry out and then they wrapped some kind of a fuse, a cord round him and he would be moaning and yelling and you could hear these moans all the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "they", who are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zenga most of all. It was Zenga who did this most of all and then Osman and Delic were there too, Kemo, all those other guards were there too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Mr. Landzo and Mr. Delic there at the time when he was burnt with a fuse or with a cord?

utterances.speaker: MS. MCMURREY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I am going to have to object because there has been no predicate laid as to whether this happened inside or outside. I would like the Prosecutor to let us know whether he has personal knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I withdraw that, your Honour. When you talk about this occasion where Mr. Vukasin Mrkajic was burned, did you observe it happening yourself?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Landzo did these things inside too. He would do it inside but he would also do it outside.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You are being asked, which of them did you see do the burnings.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I saw mostly when they took them out and they did these things and these burnings and when they come back, they were crying, Vukasin was crying that the fuse was around his body and he came back in crying and moaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: On that occasion when you saw him come out crying about the fuse that had been round his body, did you see who had taken him out on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Zenga called him out, Zenga, Zenga. He came to the door, said "come out" and that is how it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see who it was, which guard it was that actually brought him back, or was he brought back by a guard?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He flew back like a bullet being chased until the fuse dropped.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When he came back into the room, did you observe any guards either at the door or near the entrance way to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not really see all that because my back turned. Sometimes I could see, I have forgotten these things, to be quite frank with you. I really cannot recall all the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall hearing the sounds of the voices of the guards at the time of this particular incident that you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I heard Zenga, I heard him screaming at him. Others were shouting too, but Zenga most of all.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you able to recall anything that Zenga said when you heard him screaming and shouting?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall, I really cannot. I must be honest about it, I cannot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall anything that Mr. Vukasin Mrkajic may have said during the time this fuse was put around his body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was screaming, he would mention his mother "do not do this to me for God's sake", something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he call out any of the names of the guards while this was happening? Did he appeal to any of the guards and mention them by name or nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I really cannot remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you also know a person in the hangar number 6 by the name of Dusan Bendo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I know Dusan Bendo too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see anything happen to Dusan Bendo in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also he was taken out and he showed us his burns on his body. We did not dare go up to him. He would be taken out by Zenga, it was Zenga, then he would scream and wail and we saw the burns and that was it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know whether or not he was offered any medical -- this is Mr. Bendo, whether he received any medical attention for the burns he had received?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only when the Red Cross came as far as I believe -- not believe, but I think no one got any medical attention before the Red Cross. Somebody was ill, had a high temperature, maybe they may have brought him a tablet or two, but I cannot really remember. Mostly when the Red Cross came, then they went for treatment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know a man by the name of Zejnil Delalic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know him well. He had a car repair shop. I later heard that he had opened a cafe in his house. I never visited that cafe. The man was working in Germany. On one occasion, when we were in the camp somebody said, the guards would say "sit still, the commander is coming". So I sat there looking in front of me. The man entered, about five or six metres from me, now I cannot remember. I think there were two other people with him with pistols, behind them was Delic. Delic was wearing a military uniform. I cannot recall whether the others were in uniform. I do not seem to be able to recall that. The man would walk around about 10 metres and as he turned back, he was at the doorway, and Delic fired a shot with his automatic rifle which went through the steel roof and then one bullet ricocheted and hit, I think hit Kuljanin and hit him in the thigh.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did this happen, where Delic fired the bullets? Where did this happen?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It happened in the hangar. They had already made the tour and I think that Delalic had also walked out. When Delic reached the doorway, he fired this shot up into the roof.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "made the tour", the tour was made by Mr. Delalic; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I am thinking of Mr. Delalic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Delic was with Mr. Delalic at the time, was he?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was with him, he was following him, behind him when they came. Now I just cannot remember. As far as I recall one of them had a white T-shirt, but we did not really dare look up. We had to have our arms on our knees, they walked around a little, so I now really cannot recall whether he had a uniform or not. That is the truth of it, but Delic did have a uniform. He was always in uniform as far as I was able to observe, and he fired the shot.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did Mr. Delalic say or do anything in respect of Mr. Delic when the rifle was fired inside the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot recall. He may have said something, he may not have said anything, I cannot remember that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall whether Mr. Delalic did anything as a consequence of the person being wounded by the gunfire?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot, I cannot remember, I really cannot. I cannot say things that I cannot be sure about. I cannot remember the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know where the village or the town where Mr. Delalic had his premises, the car repair premises and cafe? Do you know the town?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He did not have a workshop, he had a car wash shop, and I heard later that he had opened a cafe and also he repaired tyres, as far as I can remember, and washed cars. This was just near the motel, maybe 100 metres from the hotel in Konjic, on the way out of Konjic in the direction of Mostar on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you know any members of the Delalic family?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Delalics; I think it was his uncle or his brother, Dzafo Delalic, I knew him. He was a very nice man. What happened to him during this war I do not know. He was a driver. I knew him as a child.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were a prisoner at the Celebici camp, were most of the soldiers that you saw and that you knew Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as the Celebici camp is concerned, there was only Pavo Mucic who was a Croat and -- yes, somebody else, Buric, a guard, but Buric was also correct. He even brought food from certain households. I remember him giving food to Nenad Cecez.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: While you were a prisoner at the camp, did you ever hear the sounds of military training units going on, or the training of soldiers happening in or about the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could hear around the camp, they would usually close the hangars, but we could hear applause, some kind of a hymn, I do not know what. Then there was a kind of rifle warehouse and we had to go and unload ammunition into concrete bunkers and I saw this bunker, and just behind it one could hear applause and noise, people, a lot of people gathered.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Again while you were in the camp, did you at any stage see a journalist come to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: While we were in the Celebici camp some people did come to take photographs. I know they were black. I cannot say for sure whether they were from Arab countries or from others, but I know they were black. They came several times, three or four times, I think it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did they do when they came to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came to the camp, we had to sit down. Delic would lead them. I could not really look up. He would force people to get up and put their hands behind their heads. I could not see very much what happened on that occasion.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The person that you just referred to, Hazim Delic, do you think you would recognise this gentleman again if you saw him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Hazim Delic? Of course I would, yes, I would be able to recognise him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think you could recognise the person that you have referred to as Zenga if you saw him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I would. I do not know how much he has changed in five years, but I should be able to recognise everyone. I am not so sure about Delalic, maybe less so.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Thank you. No further questions, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is there any cross-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, as we have not agreed about the order, I will start with the cross-examination of the witness, because it is our agreement if we do not have any special arrangements, we follow according to the order in the indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Proceed then. Cross-examined by MS. RESIDOVIC

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Mr. Sudar, I am Edina Residovic, I am counsel for Zejnil Delalic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sudar, as you and I speak the same language and understand each other very well, your answers to my questions can be quick. However, we are asked by the court that you should wait until after I ask you a question for the translation into the English language so that everybody in the courtroom can hear my question, and only then answer my question, and I myself will also wait for the translation and only then ask you another question. Have you understood this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Sudar, during the examination-in-chief, you said that you had lived in the village of Cerici until the war, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that you used to come to the city of Konjic until mid-April, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, somewhere around that I had transferred my wife to her relatives in Montenegro then I returned with my car. I also had intended to move my brother's wife and children, but I was returned from the road by Durak, he was there near the motel with a sort of a brigade, I am not sure what it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I do not think the witness has understood that he can hear the English translation with those other earphones, because he is not waiting until the translation and it is all starting to run together, which is what we are trying to avoid. So if he could be properly instructed in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Will you kindly tell him to wait for the translation of questions before he gives the answer?

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Sudar, you have earphones sitting on the table in front of you and you can hear the English translation. When the sound stops coming from the earphones will you only then answer my question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have understood.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You have just said, Mr. Sudar, that you are not quite sure that you are able to recognise Mr. Delalic, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only know him by sight, and I only saw him on a number of occasions when he came to the camp and we did not dare turn around, but the guards would say "here comes the commander".

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you, before the war, you never had occasion to personally meet Mr. Delalic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war I never had the opportunity to be in contact with Mr. Delalic. I never had established any contact with him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sudar, you know that in Konjic and in its surroundings there are many families bearing the same surname, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, there are many Delalics who are related.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And as you have testified before the court, you knew his brother Dzafo who immediately before the war died in Konjic. You certainly are aware of the fact that his family is also quite numerous, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether Dzafo is his brother or his uncle, I cannot say for sure. I do not know Delalic very well because he worked abroad. I saw his wife every now and then, I think she is from Belgrade, from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. What you have just testified before the court is because you heard the guards, is on the basis of what you heard the guards say and not on the basis of your personal knowledge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The guards said very plainly and clearly "here comes the commander. He is at the door". I could not see the man properly, I only saw him in passing. I cannot now remember whether he was in uniform or not. I only saw a man with a pistol in a white T-shirt, corpulent and wide built.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You can testify before this court on the basis of your personal cognisance of facts. Thank you. Mr. Sudar, please tell me when you returned to Cerici, when you were returning to Cerici, was it necessary for you to pass through the checkpoint which was in front of Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not see a checkpoint anywhere, we passed normally to Donje Selo to that side. I do not know where the checkpoint was. Checkpoint -- there was a checkpoint near the motel. There was one in the city and one towards Donje Selo. Perhaps I was intercepted, perhaps something else was the case, I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Lazar Cecez, is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, everybody knew him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he also had certain powers in terms of inspecting people coming into and leaving Donje Selo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not inspected by anyone. I was never on very friendly terms with the Cecezs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let me ask you now something in view of the fact that you testified before this court that you personally knew Mirko Babic. Please tell me whether it is correct that Mirko Babic is from Bjelasnica and he is a forester?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is true that Mirko Babic was from Bjelasnica, he worked in the carpentry department, rather in the timber department. He worked there more than he was a forest warden. I think that he was transferred to Sipad because there were more foresters than they needed, but I cannot remember exactly now.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: They used to call him Pal because he liked to socialise with people. He was a bachelor and he was on his own?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he was a bachelor. They called him, Jaranika which means Pal and he was not married.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you also know the forester Marjan Rajic, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The forester Marjan Rajic, I know him. I know Marjan Rajic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are certainly aware of the fact that several years before the war, Jaranika and Marjan Rajic had slaked some lime and they used some gas and that they had burns inflicted, serious burns on themselves?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I only hear this for the first time now madam.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I should like to ask you some other questions now. In relation to what you have testified before this court, will you please tell me, Mr. Sudar, is it true that before the war while there still existed a Yugoslavia, that the armed force of Yugoslavia was the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence Force and that the Ministry of the Secretariat of the Interior, as we call it, dealt with police and internal security affairs; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do you mean the Secretariat of the Interior? I have not understood the question well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the armed forces of the former Yugoslavia were the Yugoslav People's Army and the Territorial Defence, and the police was the SUP or the MUP as we called it; is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know. I know we had a Yugoslav Army; right before the war there appeared an army of the Muslims, or an army of the Serbs, or an army of the Croats. There appeared or emerged three armies.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the promulgation of independence of Bosnia-Herzegovina early in April, do you know that the Yugoslav People's Army then was no longer the army of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We took our oath before the authorities of the Yugoslav army and not before any other army. I do not know what to tell you. We as Serbs could not go to any other army but the one that we had taken an oath before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you know that the Territorial Defence and the MUP remained in Konjic, the ones from before the war, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I really did not take much interest in those matters. I cannot give you a precise answer.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you say that there existed in Konjic legal legitimate organs of authority in the first days of the war, an assembly, a presidency, a municipal government, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course, Konjic was a municipality and everything functioned while there was a Yugoslavia. Prior to the war, immediately before the war, all the parties -- there were divisions along the lines of parties SDA, SDS.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No, Mr. Sudar, I am not interested in these political questions. Let somebody else discuss those things. I am asking you about facts. The village of Cerici from which you come, Bjelasnica, Donje Selo is a local community, all these villages and hamlets belonged to the municipality of Konic; is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They belonged to it, of course, before normally, before the war I mean then.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I believe that they did not go anywhere from that particular area, I am referring to the villages?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The villages, there are still the villages there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know, Mr. Sudar, that in these authorities of the municipality of Konjic to which all these villages belong comprised representatives of all the nations living in Konjic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean the municipality of Konjic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, until the war.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Before the war there was mixed composition in the SUP, some people were not satisfied as far as I could see. Why that was the case I do not know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But the police force and the inspectors, the managing staff, the superiors also comprised members of all the nations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, while Yugoslavia existed there were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know Duro Kuljanin, do you not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but only slightly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: He was the vice-president of the assembly of the Konjic municipality?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what he was, I was not interested in politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But he is a Serb, is he not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I know he is a Serb, but I am not at all interested in politics.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Sudar. You spoke about events which took place somewhere around 20th May. You used some national designations. However, a while ago you said that you knew that both the Territorial Defence and the MUP were in Konjic, but you said that the HVO also appeared later?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In Konjic, in April, I saw in the town people wearing black uniforms, so I am not sure who they were, HOS people, and I also saw other people wearing fezes on their heads, you know what the army used to be before that, the Yugoslav army. Then I could not exactly tell, but these are the uniforms I saw.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This HVO army first stationed itself, as you said, in the motel and that was the reason why you no longer went to the city; is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We dared not go, but some of it -- Draganic would go to buy something and when he returned he would return black and blue, Vlado Draganic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the commander of the HVO police there was called Aga, is that a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, to tell you frankly, I do not know who was the commander nor who -- what his function was nor his name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you personally know Ivan Jozic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Ivan Jozic, let me tell you the truth, he worked at the petrol station if that is the Ivan Jozic you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Nicknamed Aga.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not Aga, perhaps you have someone else in mind. Aga was Branko Josic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And he was present when you surrendered your arms and when you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, he was not present, he was not present there as far as I could see. There for the most part were no Croats down there on the bridge but only this Jozic who worked at the gas station and most of them were Muslims and they were people unknown to me. And this Masic, I am sorry, this Masic was also there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And these are known people who arrested you, they were not the same people who you later saw at Celebici as guards?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I did not see so much of those people, I only saw them seldom. I would not know them had they not come to the prison in Konjic, Masic, for instance, and because somebody told me this is Masic and he took my wallet and my identity card and my driving licence and everything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sudar, please, is it true that you, just as all others who pass through an unpleasant experience, wish to put it behind and forget it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Madam, I would like to forget it. My father who was 70 years old was beaten at home, we heard that it was the Muslims who beat him. We had already been taken to camp, and my father went to the house of this Aga, Branko Josic, who hid him in a barn and fed him for seven days, even bringing him coffee occasionally, to prevent them from killing him. Then he returned my father home. After that he was transferred by the Croats.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you are grateful?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He saved my father.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, but I wish to ask you something else. Is it true that last year you remembered some of these events better than you can recall them right now, or that you will be able to recall them in a couple of years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Madam, I really cannot recall these things. Five years have elapsed. My father and my mother were killed in the war and I lost everything that was dear to me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you certainly remember some of the impressive things that you remember better than some other particulars?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot say. If I do remember them I shall give you an answer, of course.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For instance, if a bullet is fired in the hangar which is not quite a frequent occurrence, this is something that a man would tend to remember; is that not a fact?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You, Mr. Sudar, were heard last year in the month of February by the investigators of this Prosecutor of the International Tribunal, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion you signed the statement which you made then?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And on that occasion the translator gave you also to sign a witness acknowledgment where you stated that you had given that statement of your own accord, that you had said everything that you knew and that you were aware that statement could be used before this Tribunal, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you had no idea of who might be indicted before this court, is that so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: What do I know? I really cannot tell who might or could have been or will be indicted.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time you did not tell Mr. Sergio Oaxaca, the investigator, you did not even mention this bullet fired in the hangar and this occurrence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, I perhaps have forgotten that. Why, madam, I did not say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Had you not been directly asked about Mr. Delalic's name you would never have mentioned it; is that not so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Let me tell you, Madam, please, as you say, I did not mention it then, but did I mention then Zeljko Cecez? When I came from the hall from Celebici on the religious holiday on that evening, he was also killed then. Perhaps I did not mention Klimenta either, because I had also forgotten: Zeljko Klimenta, he too, just a few days before the Red Cross came, had been also taken out in the morning and killed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you, yes, but you stated that all the Serbs in Cerici and Donje Selo, their phone lines had been cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the telephones were down, were cut in all the villages and I heard that was not the case in my house and I dared not approach my house. I dared not go to my house because of the snipers, as my house was down by the road, by the lake and I did not dare go there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us on what date was it that the telephone lines were cut?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that took place before the attack on Donje Selo. I really cannot recall all the particulars, but it was -- everything was cut, all the lines were cut before the attack. I really cannot recall exactly. I do remember they were down.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you went to your father's, Mr. Sudar, when the attack started?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When the attack on Donje Selo started, I dare not remain overnight and sleep in my house. I only came to water the garden and then I would go and stay in the forest while the attack was on and then return.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Sudar, you did not check at all whether your own phone was functioning or not, so somebody else had to inform you of this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Madam, I told you, I just dared not sleep by the road because we walked across a slope to my father's house amid a hail storm of bullets whizzing between my and my father's house and I would just go down to water the garden and return immediately to the village, because I had no other obligations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Sudar, were you present when the interview was conducted with the President of the municipality, when the talk was conducted?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was outside, Strajo Cecez called and Slobodan were inside in my father's house and they called him on the phone and he promised him reportedly that the next day --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. And the President said that all the villagers were to surrender all the weapons in their possession?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, anyone who had any armaments were to take and they did, everybody who had some arms surrendered them as instructed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you personally also handed over your weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the piece which I had I surrendered it -- which I had bought before.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You know that many villagers in Donje Selo and Cerici had procured weapons for themselves before the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, madam. I really know very little about that thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you told the investigator of the Prosecutor's office that you know that people were selling their cows in order to procure weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Normally, naturally I did not sell my cow, I had some money put aside and I bought myself a weapon and later on I surrendered it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you have?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I bought myself a pistol and then I surrendered it later and I did not carry it. I hid it in the woods. Later when I was in the camp I told them where it was and it was found there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: After the call, the talk with the President, you testified the shelling immediately stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the shelling stopped thereafter, so they said -- a hour or so after that, towards evening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Then the morning, all of you took the weapons?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not in the morning, no, madam, the shelling stopped on the 21st, and we agreed then with the President that everybody who had arms should surrender them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you surrendered the weapons many of you wondered at the multitude of arms found in the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know, madam, maybe you do but I do not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Tell me, please, what did you see of the weapons which were surrendered on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, there was an occasional rifle. I was among the first to hand over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Automatic rifles?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whether there had been any automatic rifles, mostly they were old hunting rifles, as far as I could see.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise, just let me take a look at these papers. In Celebici, you say you were interrogated, you were hurt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were blindfolded, I can tell you, and then we were beaten up. We were unconscious and then we were taken to this judge, and I cannot really see how I can go face a judge blindfolded, I failed to really comprehend.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this on the very next day after you had been brought to the camp of Celebici?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was that same night. First we were lined up against a wall in Celebici when we arrived that night. Then we were beaten and then we were transferred to 22 and we found Babic lying there who later died. There were five or six people there also, Jovak among them, each one of them was taken out that evening and beaten up and taken to face that court blindfolded.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please tell me, do you know that the President of this panel of this commission was interrogating the men that were apprehended then was Goran Lokas, the President of the court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Madam, I could not see, I could not see him, and judging by the -- I believe that this forester Subasic I believe, judging by his accent, I heard him only utter a few -- maybe, I could not see.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I have a certain number of questions still, I do not know whether to finish it today; I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You know we have a practice of closing at 5.30. This Trial Chamber will not sit tomorrow because we have already committed that all along. It was our schedule that we were not sitting tomorrow, so you might as well wait until Monday to continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. RESIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. (5.35 pm) (Court adjourned until 10.00 am on Monday 11th August 1997) 17 18 19 20 21 22 23 24 25
